beats.text: Shown: answer in 3 sentences. Said: selection, not instruction; memory cells; 7 → 3 days
unsaid: 'answer in 3 sentences' is shown, but the Said column gives only three fragments. The reader never hears the answer as sentences.
leap: It is not said what '7 → 3 days' measures (days until what?), or what is being selected.

beats.text: Shown: pathogen numbers. Said: infection is a race; 100 particles ×10/day; symptoms above 100 million
unsaid: The 'pathogen numbers' are shown, but the words never say what the pathogen is (a virus or bacterium).
leap: 'infection is a race': only one runner is named. The reader is not told what the germ is racing against.
No reason is given for treating infection as a race.

beats.text: Shown: library numbers. Said: random receptors, >100 million kinds; 20,000 genes can't list them; loose fit + many antigens; self-binders removed
unsaid: The 'library numbers' are shown, but the words never call it a library or say what it holds. The cell that carries the receptor (lymphocyte) is never named or described.
leap: '20,000 genes can't list them': it is not said how random receptors are made from a limited number of genes.
'loose fit + many antigens': it is not said why this means some cell will fit.
excess: 'self-binders removed' is not needed for the main argument at this point.

beats.text: Shown: clone arithmetic. Said: only matching ~100 cells divide every 8 h; effector cells; why fewer can beat more
unsaid: The 'clone arithmetic' is shown, but the words do not say what a clone is or give the 1,000,000 target.
leap: Where '~100 cells' comes from, after '>100 million kinds'.
'why fewer can beat more': the reason is named but not given.

beats.text: Shown: 13.3 divisions; 7 days; 1 billion particles. Said: the clone starts tiny
unsaid: '13.3 divisions' appears with no equation and no target count in the words.
'1 billion particles' is shown, but the words do not compare it with the 100 million symptom threshold (so: sick).
leap: 13.3 divisions × 8 h is about 4.4 days, not '7 days'. The difference is not explained.

beats.text: Shown: 99% die, 1% stay: 10,000. Said: memory cells; 6.6 divisions; 3 days; 100,000 particles
unsaid: '99% die, 1% stay' is shown, but the words do not say it.
The words never say that 100,000 particles is below the symptom threshold (so: not sick).
leap: 6.6 × 8 h is about 2.2 days, not '3 days'.

beats.text: Shown: vaccine = antigen + adjuvant, no disease. Said: runs beat 4–6 safely; why adjuvant
unsaid: The 'adjuvant' is shown, but the words say only 'why adjuvant' and never explain it (no danger signal is given).
leap: It is not said why antigen alone causes no disease.

beats.text: Shown: flu vs measles. Said: antigen change; effectiveness defined
unsaid: The flu vs measles comparison is shown, but no numbers or definition of effectiveness are given in the words.
leap: It is not said why a change in antigen breaks memory (no new matching cells).
excess: The 'effectiveness defined' detail is not needed for the main argument.

beats.text: Shown: recap. Said: answer in the opening words; cache analogy and where it breaks
leap: A new analogy appears at the very end, and its content and where it breaks are not given.
excess: 'answer in the opening words' repeats Beat 1.

question.text: How can a vaccine prepare the body for a germ it has never met?
question.known_at: Never stated in Said/Shown. Beat 1 only implies it through the answer.
question.result_stated: Only in compressed form, Beat 1: 'selection, not instruction; memory cells; 7 → 3 days'

reply.motive: Missing from the beats. 'sounds impossible' appears only in the plan. A reason for the approach is also missing: Beat 2 asserts 'infection is a race' with no reason.
reply.close: Beat 9: 'answer in the opening words'. The answer is not quoted, and the general argument (each doubling of starting cells saves one 8 h division) is not stated in the beats.
reply.recap: Your body already has a few cells that fit a germ by chance; a vaccine multiplies them safely once, so next time there are many more and the race is won in about 3 days instead of about 7.
reply.strongest: Beats 5–6: the same arithmetic, 100 vs 10,000 starting cells, gives 13.3 vs 6.6 divisions and 1 billion vs 100,000 particles.
reply.weakest: Beat 3: four undefined terms ('receptors', 'antigens', 'self-binders', 'library') arrive at once, and the cell carrying the receptor is never named.
suggestions: Name the second runner in Beat 2: immune cells that must multiply to fight back.
Define lymphocyte, receptor and antigen in plain words in Beat 3.
Say the 1,000,000 target and the 100×2^n equation aloud, and explain why 4.4 days becomes 7 (start-up delay).
Explain the adjuvant as the 'this is a threat' signal.
State the question and why it seems impossible at the start of Beat 1.
